newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X slides in Busang deal aftermath.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X slides in Busang deal aftermath.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd dropped in heavy trading again on Monday as the market struggled to place a value on the Calgary company after its deal with Louisiana-based Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia.
Bre-X fell 1.30 to 19.90 by midday in Toronto with more than two million shares trading hands. The stock has fallen steadily since last Thursday, when it closed at 22.70.
Part of the slide stemmed from comments from Placer Dome Inc officials late last week that indicated the company had no further interest in Bre-X, analysts said.
"We don't see an opportunity for a meaningful role...we don't see any way in for us," Placer chief executive John Willson told reporters in a conference call on Thursday.

Placer earlier dropped its US$5 billion merger offer for Bre-X after Bre-X announced its deal with Freeport. The Freeport arrangement left Bre-X with 45 percent of the deposit, down from 90 percent. Freeport will control 15 percent of Busang and be the operator. Indonesian interests will control the rest of the project.
Placer said that since the deal handed operator status to Freeport, Bre-X was no longer an attractive target.
"People don't really know where Bre-X stands now," said gold analyst Catherine Gignac with Deacon Capital.

Gignac said Bre-X had the largest share of the deposit, yet had no control over developing the mine. She added that its Indonesian partners, led by business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, were playing a role in the mine development that seemed bigger than their 30 percent would call for.
"We don't know what their strategy is," she said. "The confusion has not disappeared yet."
Analysts are also struggling over how to place a value on Bre-X shares.
"There's a big argument on how much it's worth," said gold analyst Michael Fowler with Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion.

North American gold companies traditionally trade at a large premium to their net asset values. But Bre-X, as a non-operating majority partner, might not garner the same premium as North American gold producers, analysts said.
They said they did not expect any major developments with Bre-X until the company received its contracts of work from the Indonesian government, expected at the end of March.
"A lot of mystery's been taken out of the stock," said one trader.
